title: Pseudo-coherence is independent of the finite polynomial presentation
statement: Let $R,A$ be commutative rings and let $r,s\geq0$. Suppose $\alpha:P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $\beta:Q=R[y_1,\ldots,y_s]\twoheadrightarrow A$ are surjective $R$-algebra homomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For every $K\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], its restriction of scalars $\alpha_*K\in D(P)$ is pseudo-coherent if and only if its restriction of scalars $\beta_*K\in D(Q)$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Here restriction of scalars keeps the additive groups and differentials of a representing complex, with scalar action through the displayed map; no boundedness, flatness, finite presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed beyond the two finite polynomial surjections.

source.place: Tag 065H, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent, pseudo-coherent clause (some presentation if and only if every presentation).

proof.text: For any commutative ring $B$ and $b\in B$, let $e_b:B[t]\to B$ be evaluation at $b$. There is an exact sequence $0\to B[t]\xrightarrow{t-b}B[t]\xrightarrow{e_b}B\to0$. Indeed evaluation is surjective on constants; $p(t)-p(b)$ is divisible by $t-b$, since $t^i-b^i=(t-b)\sum_{j=0}^{i-1}t^{i-1-j}b^j$ for $i>0$. Multiplication by $t-b$ is injective: for a nonzero polynomial its highest nonzero coefficient remains the highest coefficient after multiplication, in degree one higher. Thus the complex $[B[t]\xrightarrow{t-b}B[t]]$ in degrees $-1,0$, augmented by $e_b$, is a bounded finite free resolution of $B[0]$. In particular $B[0]$ is pseudo-coherent over $B[t]$, including when $B$ is the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 065G, lemma-add-variable-pseudo-coherent, first proof paragraph; translated from t to t-b by the displayed elementary calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-pseudocoherent-algebra-scalar-restriction] to $e_b:B[t]\to B$. Its sole algebra hypothesis is exactly the pseudo-coherence of $B[0]$ established in step 1. Consequently, for every $L\in D(B)$, $L$ is pseudo-coherent over $B$ if and only if $(e_b)_*L$ is pseudo-coherent over $B[t]$. This assertion is uniform in $B,b,L$ and requires no cohomological bound on $L$.

source.place: Tag 064Z, lemma-finite-push-pseudo-coherent, final assertion; Tag 065G, lemma-add-variable-pseudo-coherent

proof.text: Choose $f_j\in P$ with $\alpha(f_j)=\beta(y_j)$ and $g_i\in Q$ with $\beta(g_i)=\alpha(x_i)$, using the two surjections. Put $T=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s]$. Evaluation gives $u:T\to P$ fixing every $x_i$ and sending $y_j\mapsto f_j$, and $v:T\to Q$ fixing every $y_j$ and sending $x_i\mapsto g_i$. The universal property of the polynomial ring gives $\gamma:=\alpha\circ u=\beta\circ v$, since the two maps agree on $R$ and every variable. The same universal property identifies $T$ both with $P[y_1,\ldots,y_s]$ and with $Q[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$: the maps fixing each displayed variable are inverse. Restriction along a composite keeps the identical groups and differentials with the identical composite scalar action, so $u_*\alpha_*K=\gamma_*K=v_*\beta_*K$.

source.place: Tag 065H, lemma-relatively-pseudo-coherent, choice of lifts and the common polynomial ring diagram

proof.text: For $0\le j\le s$ set $P_j=P[y_1,\ldots,y_j]$ and give a representative of $\alpha_*K$ the $P_j$-action $y_a\mapsto f_a$ for $a\le j$. The $j$th action is restriction of the $(j-1)$st along $P_{j-1}[y_j]\to P_{j-1}$ evaluating $y_j$ at $f_j\in P\subset P_{j-1}$. Induct on $j$: at $j=0$ the complex is $\alpha_*K$; each successor uses the uniform equivalence of step 2, hence preserves and reflects pseudo-coherence. At $j=s$ this gives $\alpha_*K$ pseudo-coherent over $P$ if and only if $\gamma_*K$ is pseudo-coherent over $T$. Likewise take $Q_i=Q[x_1,\ldots,x_i]$, start at $\beta_*K$, and evaluate $x_i$ at $g_i\in Q\subset Q_{i-1}$. Induction for $0\le i\le r$ gives $\beta_*K$ pseudo-coherent over $Q$ if and only if the same $\gamma_*K$ is pseudo-coherent over $T$. Combining the equivalences proves the assertion. If $s=0$ or $r=0$ the corresponding induction is the identity equivalence.
